text:
alex: Heads-up — we saw a 3x spike in spot interruptions in us-west-2 during last night's maintenance window. Thinking we should tweak the autoscaler & fallback policy for spot-backed inference fleets. Proposal below.

irina: What did the failure mode look like? Mostly cold starts, or request retries/backpressure?

marc: Main problems: KV-cache cold-warm cycles, request queue growth, and retries causing thundering. When spots get evicted we simultaneously lose KV caches and then flood the remaining nodes with cache misses — latency tails blow up.

priya: For SLOs, I'd rather a controlled fallback to on-demand than an uncontrolled meltdown. Two levers: smarter scale-out triggers + a conservative cooldown/surge control so we don't overprovision spot during transient blips.

jenny: Can we define a mixed-pool baseline? e.g., keep 10% minimum on-demand capacity per region so critical requests always have a stable pool. Let spot be the burst capacity.

alex: Exactly. Draft autoscaler snippet (conceptual):
```yaml
autoscaler: 
  min_replicas: 20           # baseline across mixed pool
  max_replicas: 200
  scale_out_triggers:
    - metric: request_queue_length
      threshold: 50
    - metric: gpu_utilization
      threshold: 0.75
  cooldowns:
    scale_out: 90s           # wait for KV warmups to stabilize before another add
    scale_down: 300s
  surge_control:
    max_surge_percent: 25   # limit transient over-provisioning on spot
  interruption_policy:
    smoothing_window: 5m    # moving avg for predicted interruption rate
    switch_to_on_demand_when_predicted_rate_gt: 0.05
    preemptive_actions: [cordon, drain, evict_after: 30s]
  cost_guardrails:
    spike_budget: 2         # allow up to 2 on-demand adds/min unless SLO breach
```

marc: A few clarifications: smoothing_window should be a weighted moving avg so a single false positive doesn't flip us. Preemptive drain should allow inflight requests to finish (short wait) then reject new low-priority traffic.

priya: Concern: immediate scale-to-on-demand causes cost jumps. spike_budget idea is good — also add hysteresis: require SLO breach OR sustained predicted_rate > threshold for 2 consecutive windows to fully switch.

irina: We'll need metrics: spot_interruption_rate, queued_requests_per_model, kv_cache_hit_rate, inflight_token_count, add_node_duration. Wire these into the Console dashboards and attach an alert for rapid queue growth + cache hit drop.

spot-bot: [automated] Detected planned maintenance in us-west-2 on 2025-05-12T01:00Z. Predicted interruption spike: 12%.

jenny: Also consider routing lower-priority requests to smaller quantized models or a degraded path during pressure. That keeps premium SLOs intact without expensive on-demand adds.

alex: Agreed. Pilot plan for next week in us-west-2: implement mixed-pool autoscaler with surge_control=25%, cooldown=90s, smoothing_window=5m, spike_budget=2. Actions: marc -> implement scaler + canary; irina -> dashboards/alerts; priya -> SLO thresholds & cost pager. Tagging @marc @irina @priya

marc: On it. Will push a canary with 2 AZs, surge_limit 25%, cooldown 90s. Will add a k8s hook to cordon spot nodes and wait 30s for inflight to drain before eviction. PR in a few hours.

priya: I'll add a cost alert: projected on-demand delta > $120/hr -> page on-call. Also set a soft Slack-only alert at $40/hr.

irina: I'll add KV-cache warmup metric (cache_hit_rate by node age) and chart tail latency vs node add time.

alex: Nice. If this canary looks stable we roll to eu-west-1 and us-east-1.

jenny: :rocket:

alex: :thumbsup:
